references.text: The people answered Moses with a single promise to do all that the Lord had said, just as the Israelites here pledge to serve the Lord and obey his voice.
At the Sinai covenant, the people unanimously answered that they would do all that the Lord had said, a similar covenant commitment as in Joshua.
Moses read the Book of the Covenant to the people, and they promised to obey all that the Lord had said, parallel to the people's pledge to Joshua.
The people asked Moses to hear God's words and convey them, and promised to obey, the same commitment to obedience toward the Lord's voice.
The command to fear the Lord, serve him, and swear by his name reflects the same commitment to serve the Lord alone.
The instruction to fear the Lord, serve him, hold fast to him, and swear by his name is parallel to the people's pledge to serve the Lord.
Earlier in the same chapter, the people confirm their choice to serve the Lord, which is reinforced in verse 24.
Samuel challenges the people to fear the Lord, serve him, and obey his voice, the same elements found in Joshua's covenant renewal.
Samuel urges the people to fear the Lord and serve him faithfully with all their heart, a similar pledge of loyalty.
